title: Labeled pullbacks and covering sieves of the internal action category
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(C,J)$ be a $\mathcal V$-small site with finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $K:C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Grp}$ be a sheaf of groups with $\mathcal V$-small values. The objects, arrows, identities and composition specified by $\operatorname{Ob}(C_K)=\operatorname{Ob}(C)$, $\operatorname{Hom}_{C_K}(V,U)=\coprod_{f:V\to U}K(V)$, $1_U=(1_U,1)$ and $(f,a)\circ(g,b)=(fg,b\,g^*a)$ form a $\mathcal V$-small category. Projection to $C$ is a functor, and $(1_U,a)$ has inverse $(1_U,a^{-1})$. For $f:V\to U$, $g:W\to U$, $a\in K(V)$ and $b\in K(W)$, any base pullback $P=V\times_U W$, with projections $p,q$, gives a pullback in $C_K$ with legs $(p,1)$ and $(q,p^*a\,(q^*b)^{-1})$.

Let $\mathcal P_K$ consist of families $\{(f_i,a_i):U_i\to U\}$ whose underlying families $\{f_i\}$ are $J$-coverings. It contains every singleton isomorphism family and admits covering pullbacks along every arrow, for some choice of pullbacks. Every such family is isomorphic on its sources to the family $\{(f_i,1)\}$ via $(1_{U_i},a_i)$, with $(f_i,a_i)=(f_i,1)\circ(1_{U_i},a_i)$.

For Grothendieck topologies use [def-weil-pbc-topos]. A sieve means a collection of arrows with fixed target closed under precomposition. For every $U$, the map $S\mapsto S_1$, where $S_1=\{f:V\to U\mid(f,1)\in S\}$, is an order isomorphism from sieves on $U$ in $C_K$ to sieves on $U$ in $C$. Its inverse sends a base sieve $T$ to $\{(f,a)\mid f\in T\}$. It takes maximal sieves to maximal sieves, takes pullback along $(g,b)$ to pullback along $g$, preserves the local-character axiom for covering sieves, and takes the sieve generated by a family to the sieve generated by its underlying family. Consequently the Grothendieck topology generated by $\mathcal P_K$ is exactly the collection of sieves $S$ for which $S_1$ covers in the Grothendieck topology generated by $J$. No closure of $\mathcal P_K$ under presieve bind composition is asserted.

proof.text: The universe convention [def-weil-size-convention] bounds both the objects and all arrows of $C$. The set of arrows of $C_K$ is the dependent sum $\coprod_{V,U\in\operatorname{Ob}(C)}\coprod_{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_C(V,U)}K(V)$, hence belongs to $\mathcal V$ by closure under indexed sums in a Grothendieck universe. The object set is unchanged, so $C_K$ is $\mathcal V$-small. Lean implementation: reuse Object K and Arrow K from InternalActionSiteBasic; their universe u already expresses this size bound.

source.place: Agent construction: smallness; the universe convention of def-weil-size-convention.

proof.text: Write $f:V\to U$, $g:W\to V$, $h:T\to W$, and choose labels $a\in K(V)$, $b\in K(W)$, $c\in K(T)$. The two associative composites have base $fgh$ and labels $c\,h^*(b\,g^*a)$ and $(c\,h^*b)(gh)^*a$, respectively; these agree since restrictions are group homomorphisms and $(gh)^*=h^*g^*$. The left and right identity laws reduce to $a1=a$, $1a=a$ and identity restriction. Thus the specified data form a category; forgetting the label preserves both identities and composition. Lean implementation: reuse the existing category instance and projection, whose identity and composition data are exactly these formulas. No second category is constructed.

source.place: Agent construction: category laws, using only group and functor axioms.

proof.text: Both composites of $(1_U,a)$ and $(1_U,a^{-1})$ equal $(1_U,1)$, since their labels are $a^{-1}a$ and $aa^{-1}$. More generally $(f,a)=(f,1)\circ(1_V,a)$ for $f:V\to U$. Thus replacing each source $U_i$ by the automorphism $(1_{U_i},a_i)$ gives exactly the claimed isomorphism of families, without any assertion about closure of coverings under replacement.

source.place: Agent construction: vertical inverses and normalization of families.

proof.text: For $f:V\to U$, $g:W\to U$, labels $a,b$, and a base pullback $(P,p,q)$, put $k=p^*a\,(q^*b)^{-1}$. The proposed legs $(p,1)$ and $(q,k)$ have equal composites to $U$: their bases are $fp=gq$ and their labels are $p^*a$ and $kq^*b=p^*a$. This verifies the pullback square's commutativity with the stated multiplication order.

source.place: Agent construction: labeled pullback square, commutativity.

proof.text: Given a cone $(r,c):T\to V$, $(s,d):T\to W$ over the same arrows, its equality of composites says $fr=gs$ and $c\,r^*a=d\,s^*b$. There is a unique base map $t:T\to P$ with $pt=r$, $qt=s$. The arrow $(t,c)$ has first leg $(r,c)$ and second leg $(s,c\,t^*k)=(s,c\,r^*a(s^*b)^{-1})=(s,d)$. Any other lift $(t',e)$ has $t'=t$ by the base pullback property and $e=c$ by its first leg, proving uniqueness. This proves the universal property, including for noncommutative $K(T)$. Lean reuses the shared CategoryTheory.InternalActionSite.labeled_pullback theorem, whose original geometry proof is relocated unchanged in substance to InternalActionSiteBasic. The shared arrow_ext proof is relocated there too; neither result is reproved here.

source.place: Agent construction: labeled pullback universal property.

proof.text: For an isomorphism $(f,a)$ in $C_K$, projection sends its inverse to an inverse of $f$. Hence $\{f\}$ is a $J$-covering by the isomorphism axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and $\{(f,a)\}\in\mathcal P_K$. For a family in $\mathcal P_K$ and an arrow $(g,b):W\to U$, use the base site's pullback axiom to choose $P_i=U_i\times_UW$ so that $\{q_i:P_i\to W\}$ covers. Steps 4--5 give pullbacks with legs to $W$ labeled $p_i^*a_i(q_i^*b)^{-1}$. Their underlying family is precisely $\{q_i\}$, so they belong to $\mathcal P_K$. Only the some-choice pullback axiom of Tag 00VH (definition-site, clarification after the definition) is used; arbitrary isomorphic replacement of base covers is unnecessary. In Lean, image_presieve identifies the existential-label image with Presieve.map (projection K), so precoverage_eq identifies the given precoverage with J.comap (projection K). The already imported theorem CategoryTheory.InternalActionSite.hasIsos supplies isomorphism covers; covering_family_iff and labeled_pullback lift precisely the covering pullbacks chosen by hJ.2.2.

source.place: Tag 00VH, definition-site and its clarification: singleton isomorphism covers and some choice of covering pullbacks; apply the explicit pullbacks of steps 4--5.

proof.text: Let $S$ be a sieve as defined in [def-weil-pbc-topos]. Precomposition with $(1_V,a)$ and $(1_V,a^{-1})$ gives $(f,1)\in S\Longleftrightarrow(f,a)\in S$. Precomposition of $(f,1)$ by $(g,1)$ then proves $S_1$ is a base sieve. Conversely $T_K:=\{(f,a)\mid f\in T\}$ is a sieve whenever $T$ is a base sieve, since a composite has base $fg$. The equivalence of membership just proved gives $(S_1)_K=S$ and $(T_K)_1=T$. Both assignments preserve inclusion, giving the asserted order isomorphism; the full sieve is carried to the full sieve. Implemented by the proved private helpers label_iff, baseSieve, liftSieve and sieveEquiv; baseSieve proves its downward closure directly, without using the unfinished labelOne_downward theorem.

source.place: Tag 00Z4, definition-topology; direct verification for the agent-defined labeled category, not a theorem quoted from Stacks.

proof.text: For $(g,b):W\to U$ and any $h:T\to W$, $h\in((g,b)^*S)_1$ means $(g,b)\circ(h,1)=(gh,h^*b)\in S$. By step 7 this is equivalent to $gh\in S_1$, namely $h\in g^*(S_1)$. Thus $((g,b)^*S)_1=g^*(S_1)$, and equivalently $(g,b)^*(T_K)=(g^*T)_K$. These equalities use exactly the pullback-sieve definition in [def-weil-pbc-topos], not existence or preservation of categorical pullbacks.

source.place: Tag 00Z4, definition-topology; direct verification for the agent-defined labeled category, not a theorem quoted from Stacks.

proof.text: For a family $F=\{(f_i,a_i)\}$, define its generated sieve to consist of all composites $(f_i,a_i)\circ(h,c)$: this is a sieve, contains $F$, and is contained in every sieve containing $F$. Its base arrows factor through some $f_i$. Conversely, if $f=f_ih$ and $a\in K(\operatorname{dom}h)$, then $(f,a)=(f_i,a_i)\circ(h,a(h^*a_i)^{-1})$. Therefore $\langle F\rangle=(\langle\{f_i\}\rangle)_K$. This argument also applies when the family is empty: both generated sieves are empty.

source.place: Tag 00Z4, definition-topology; direct verification for the agent-defined labeled category, not a theorem quoted from Stacks.

proof.text: For any base Grothendieck topology $H$, declare $S$ covering on $C_K$ exactly when $S_1\in H$. Maximality and pullback stability follow from steps 7--8 and the axioms in [def-weil-pbc-topos]. For local character, let $S$ cover and suppose $(f,a)^*R$ covers for every $(f,a)\in S$. Taking $a=1$ for each $f\in S_1$ shows $f^*R_1\in H$ by step 8; local character of $H$ yields $R_1\in H$. Thus these declarations form a topology $\Phi(H)$.

source.place: Tag 00Z4, definition-topology; direct verification for the agent-defined labeled category, not a theorem quoted from Stacks.

proof.text: Conversely, for any topology $L$ on $C_K$ declare a base sieve $T$ covering when $T_K\in L$. Maximality and pullback stability follow using $(g,1)$ in step 8. If $T_K$ covers and $(f^*R)_K$ covers for each $f\in T$, then for every $(f,a)\in T_K$ step 8 gives $(f,a)^*(R_K)=(f^*R)_K\in L$. Local character in $L$ gives $R_K\in L$, proving the base local-character axiom of [def-weil-pbc-topos]. Denote this topology by $\Psi(L)$. Step 7 implies $\Psi\Phi(H)=H$ and $\Phi\Psi(L)=L$; both operations preserve inclusion of covering-sieve sets.

source.place: Tag 00Z4, definition-topology; direct verification for the agent-defined labeled category, not a theorem quoted from Stacks.

proof.text: The topology generated by any prescribed collection of sieves exists: intersect all topologies containing that collection. The collection of such topologies is a set because the category is small; it is nonempty because declaring all sieves covering satisfies the three axioms of [def-weil-pbc-topos]. An intersection satisfies maximality and pullback stability componentwise; if its local-character hypotheses hold, they hold in every component topology, so the conclusion belongs to the intersection too. Hence this construction has precisely the least-topology property. For a collection of families, apply it to their generated sieves. The Lean proof uses Mathlib Precoverage.toGrothendieck_eq_sInf and generate_mem_toGrothendieck; it does not reconstruct the intersection.

source.place: Tag 00Z4, definition-topology; direct verification for the agent-defined labeled category, not a theorem quoted from Stacks.

proof.text: Let $H_J$ be the topology generated by the base $J$-covering families and $L_K$ that generated by $\mathcal P_K$. Step 9 shows that $\Phi(H_J)$ contains every generating sieve for $L_K$, so $L_K\subseteq\Phi(H_J)$. Conversely, for any topology $L$ containing those generators, each base $J$-cover has its label-one lift in $\mathcal P_K$; step 9 implies its generated base sieve lies in $\Psi(L)$. By the least property in step 12, $H_J\subseteq\Psi(L)$ and hence $\Phi(H_J)\subseteq L$ by step 11. Take $L=L_K$. Thus $L_K=\Phi(H_J)$, exactly the claimed covering-sieve criterion. No composition axiom for the family precoverage is required. Implemented by generated_topology: compare the generated topology with topologyUp, and compare the base generated topology with topologyDown of the twisted generated topology; the sieve order isomorphism turns the second comparison into the opposite inclusion. No use of the unfinished topology_mem_iff theorem.

lean.statement: theorem sieve_geometry [HasFiniteLimits C] (J : Precoverage C) (hJ : J.IsSiteForCoverings) (hK : Presheaf.IsSheaf J.toGrothendieck (K ⋙ forget GrpCat.{u})) : (∀ (X : Object K) (a : K.obj (op X.base)), (Arrow.mk (𝟙 X.base) a : X ⟶ X) ≫ Arrow.mk (𝟙 X.base) a⁻¹ = 𝟙 X ∧ (Arrow.mk (𝟙 X.base) a⁻¹ : X ⟶ X) ≫ Arrow.mk (𝟙 X.base) a = 𝟙 X) ∧ (∀ (X Y : Object K) (f : X ⟶ Y), ∃ e : X ≅ X, e.hom = Arrow.mk (𝟙 X.base) f.label ∧ e.inv = Arrow.mk (𝟙 X.base) f.label⁻¹ ∧ f = e.hom ≫ Arrow.mk f.base 1) ∧ (∀ (U V W P : Object K) (f : V ⟶ U) (g : W ⟶ U) (p : P.base ⟶ V.base) (q : P.base ⟶ W.base), IsPullback p q f.base g.base → IsPullback (Arrow.mk p 1 : P ⟶ V) (Arrow.mk q (K.map p.op f.label * (K.map q.op g.label)⁻¹) : P ⟶ W) f g) ∧ (precoverage K J).HasIsos ∧ (∀ (I : Type u) (X : Object K) (U : I → Object K) (a : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X), Presieve.ofArrows U a ∈ precoverage K J X → ∀ (Y : Object K) (b : Y ⟶ X), ∃ (P : I → Object K) (p : ∀ i, P i ⟶ Y) (q : ∀ i, P i ⟶ U i), (∀ i, IsPullback (p i) (q i) b (a i)) ∧ Presieve.ofArrows P p ∈ precoverage K J Y) ∧ ∃ e : ∀ X : Object K, Sieve X ≃o Sieve X.base, (∀ (X : Object K) (S : Sieve X) (Y : C) (f : Y ⟶ X.base), e X S f ↔ S (Arrow.mk f 1)) ∧ (∀ (X : Object K) (T : Sieve X.base) (Y : Object K) (f : Y ⟶ X), (e X).symm T f ↔ T f.base) ∧ (∀ X : Object K, e X ⊤ = ⊤) ∧ (∀ (X Y : Object K) (f : Y ⟶ X) (S : Sieve X), e Y (S.pullback f) = (e X S).pullback f.base) ∧ (∀ (X : Object K) (I : Type u) (U : I → Object K) (a : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X), e X (Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows U a)) = Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows (fun i ↦ (U i).base) (fun i ↦ (a i).base))) ∧ (∀ H : GrothendieckTopology C, ∃ L : GrothendieckTopology (Object K), ∀ (X : Object K) (S : Sieve X), S ∈ L X ↔ e X S ∈ H X.base) ∧ (∀ L : GrothendieckTopology (Object K), ∃ H : GrothendieckTopology C, ∀ (X : Object K) (T : Sieve X.base), T ∈ H X.base ↔ (e X).symm T ∈ L X) ∧ (∀ (X : Object K) (S : Sieve X), S ∈ topology K J X ↔ e X S ∈ J.toGrothendieck X.base)
